parsed.explanation: Thin dossier. Positives: nothing in criminal law addresses being trans, no presentation or morality offence, no documented border, screening, police or facility practice targeting trans visitors, and no domestic prison system (sentences served abroad) so the custody-placement axis is largely inoperative. Negatives are climate and the absence of any recourse: the governing religious institution's 2019 educational document and 2024 declaration frame 'gender theory' as 'extremely dangerous' and sex-change interventions as a dignity threat, officials have refused gay envoys, and in 2021 the foreign ministry objected to a neighbour's gender-identity hate-speech provision. There is no anti-discrimination law, no complaint mechanism and no legal gender recognition (the latter a resident gap, and the visitor carries a home passport). No documented trans visitor was stopped, refused entry or refused service; facility rules are an open question, not an exposure. Extrapolating: severe law-based harm is unlikely, but an outed visitor faces official disapprobation with no remedy — social/institutional hostility without documented violence puts this below the acceptance-with-protections tier but above jurisdictions documenting recurring visitor-facing harms.
